accessibility.labeling: The accessible name is the label of the Field that frames the combobox, or its own label where no Field does; a filled or outlined combobox draws that name floating, and labelHidden only stops the drawing. The placeholder is never the name. The description is what the Field gives: its supporting text with, in error, the error text after it and its optional text. The combobox is exposed as invalid while error is true or its Field is in error, as required while its Field says so — whichever mark is drawn — and as read-only while readOnly is true. It is expanded while its list is open, and names its active option. Its name also names the list and the chevron's button. An option is named by its label and described by its supporting text, and exposes whether it is the chosen one, whether it is disabled, and its position among the options shown; a group is named by its title. The clear button is named by clearLabel. The status row is a live region. The leading glyphs, the check and the dividers are decorative.
notes: The pattern is the WAI-ARIA editable combobox with a listbox popup: focus stays in the input and the active option is its active descendant on the web, as the search's suggestions are (SRC-14) and a select's options. The input keeps its name, its description, its invalid and required states and its focused edge while the person reads the options, and typing never stops editing the text.

Text entry happens in the platform's native text element: on the web an <input type="text" role="combobox"> in the shadow root with the label, the description and the states set on that element — not through ElementInternals, which axe cannot see.

While an input method composes, every key is the input method's (CMB-16): the Enter that confirms a conversion chooses nothing and submits nothing. A combobox that chose on that Enter cannot be used in Japanese, Chinese or Korean.

With allowCustomValue false, typing makes the first match active, so that Enter chooses what was found; a screen reader then reads that option after each change of the text. With allowCustomValue true nothing is active until an arrow key is pressed, so that Enter keeps what was typed. One rule in both: Enter commits what the field shows as about to be committed.
Leaving the field never chooses the active option (CMB-29): a pointer that rested on a row, or the first match of half a word, is not an answer. A whole label typed out is.
Escape closes, then restores, and never clears (CMB-30). Clearing is emptying the text, or the clear button.
The list does not open on focus (CMB-21): tabbing through a form would open a list over the next fields at every stop, and on a touch screen a list would rise together with the keyboard.

Errors are words: a text that names no option is given up, not kept as an error of the combobox's own, and the combobox reports no refusal to its Field (CMB-61); a product that wants to say "choose one from the list" sets error and errorText on the Field, or on the combobox field, from its change and input handlers.
A match is marked by weight (CMB-38), never by color alone and never announced: the label is read whole.
The chevron is a button for a pointer and for touch exploration, outside the focus order; the keyboard opens the list with Down Arrow.
Heights are minimums: at 200% text size the field grows, labels, options and titles wrap, and the list scrolls; only the text in the input stays on one line, and scrolls.
Web: a touch browser zooms the page into an input whose text is smaller than 16 px. Both sizes use 16 px text (comp.input-box.input.typescale.medium).

The combobox draws no frame: the label row, the requirement, the supporting row and the error are those of the Field that frames it (FLD-2 to FLD-13), and the combobox field is that pair as one component. A bare combobox is for a place whose label stands elsewhere — a toolbar, a table cell, a row of an editor — and is named by its own label. The list is an anchored surface by Popover's rules (POP-2 to POP-8, POP-18 to POP-27, POP-34, POP-36, POP-43) with the menu's look; it is not a Popover element, because its content is rows with one meaning, not content of any kind.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

The box is the combobox's own part, not a Text input placed in it: the native text element is itself the combobox — it carries the role, the expanded state and the relations to the list and to the active option, which must stand in one tree with it — and the keys, the text a choice writes and the commit are the combobox's. Its drawing is the box every input control is drawn on, from the one set of tokens `comp.input-box` that the text input, the select, the number input and the color input read too (CMB-63): the two are one drawing, and neither is built from the other.

WCAG 2.5.8 (target size): for touch every option is at least the touch target high in both densities (CMB-34). The compact density is lower than the pointer target for a fine pointer, by design: it is the density of a tool used with a mouse, it stays above the 24 by 24 the criterion asks, and its options reach across the list's whole width. A product that cannot accept that uses regular.

It draws nothing itself. `tanrei-option` and `tanrei-option-group` are one pair of elements for the select and the combobox, defined once; an option with the empty value is refused by the combobox (CMB-17, CMB-57), not by the element, because a select allows it.

web.notes: Lagging: the element in the repository still draws its own label row, requirement mark and supporting row and has the ten props of a frame; the bare control without them is not built on this platform yet. As specified: `tanrei-combobox`, class `TanreiCombobox`, React `Combobox`. A form-associated custom element (`static formAssociated = true`): it takes `name`, submits `value` (never the uncommitted text), restores it on navigation, resets to the `value` attribute, follows `<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while its Field says it is required (CMB-59); its two calls on `ElementInternals` and its form for Enter go through the shared composing primitives, so that a composed element that holds it can be the form's control in its place. The options are `<tanrei-option>` and `<tanrei-option-group>` children, observed for changes; the combobox reads them and renders the rows itself in its shadow root, so that the `<input role="combobox">`, its `aria-controls` listbox and its `aria-activedescendant` option are in one tree. **Options through a slot**: a `<slot>` element among its children stands for the elements assigned to it, flattened (`assignedElements({ flatten: true })`), in the slot's place among the other children; the combobox reads them as its own options, reads again on that slot's `slotchange`, and observes each assigned element as it observes a child. This is `readOptions()` and `OptionsController` in `primitives/option-list.ts`, shared with the select, and it is how a composed element gives the combobox the product's options without moving or copying an element. The input carries `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-readonly`, with `autocomplete="off"`, `autocapitalize="none"` and `spellcheck="false"`; its name, its description and its invalid and required states are values — its own `label`, or what the Field's connection gives (`packages/web/src/primitives/field.ts`) — written on the input as `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`, because an id cannot be referenced across a shadow root. To that connection the combobox says that it draws the label (a filled or outlined variant) and its inset (CMB-61), and takes from it `labelHidden` and the required mark besides. Composition is read from `compositionstart` / `compositionend` and `event.isComposing` (and `keyCode 229`), and keys are ignored while it lasts. The chevron is a `<button tabindex="-1" aria-label aria-expanded>` and the clear button a `<tanrei-button variant="text" size="small">`; `pointerdown` on a row, the chevron or the list calls `preventDefault` so that focus stays in the input. The list is a manual popover in the top layer, placed with CSS anchor positioning and a script fallback, sized to the anchor's width and followed with the `FollowController` the menu uses, with the combobox's own light dismiss so that `toggle` carries a reason; the element itself is the opener, so a press on the label row of a Field around it is a press outside (CMB-30). On a touch device `visualViewport` gives the keyboard's edge. The match is a `<mark>` with `background: none` and a heavier `font-weight`, inside the option's one text node sequence, which assistive technology reads as one label. `input` is the native composed event (the text is `inputValue`); the combobox sets its own `value` before firing `change` (a composed, bubbling CustomEvent whose `detail` holds `value` and `inputValue`) and its own `open` before firing `toggle` (`detail` holds `open` and `reason`), a CustomEvent that is composed and does not bubble, as the platform's own `toggle` does not. The element in the repository fires a `toggle` that is neither yet, and an event that is not composed never leaves the shadow root of an element that holds the combobox. Attributes are kebab-case (`input-value`, `label-hidden`, `allow-custom-value`, `clear-label`, `status-text`, `empty-text`) except `readonly`; a boolean attribute cannot default to true, so the web names the inverse of chevron: `no-chevron`. The `leading-icon` slot is a named slot. The `inline` attribute draws an open list in place under the box, for the fixtures. Parts: `container`, `outline`, `active-indicator`, `label` and `requirement-label` (the floating label and its asterisk), `input`, `leading-icon`, `clear-button`, `chevron`, `list`, `option`, `option-label`, `option-supporting-text`, `option-leading-icon`, `mark`, `group`, `group-title`, `divider`, `status`. Before the element is defined its options are running text: a page hides them with `tanrei-combobox:not(:defined) > * { display: none }` and gives the tag a block size. A `<datalist>` is not used: its list takes no token, no supporting text, no group and no status, and browsers disagree on how it filters. Words: the element has no words of its own. `empty-text` and `clear-label` left empty read the product's words, set once with `setWords()` from `@tanrei/web`; the element draws again when they change.

The first argument is its name, floated in a filled or outlined look; `labelHidden` follows `.labelsHidden()`, `disabled` follows `.disabled(_:)`, `action` is `onSubmit:`. Built on `TextField`; composition is the marked text of the field, during which the component handles no key. The list is Tanrei's, presented as TanreiMenu's surface is, without taking focus.
